title: Semantics of the rejection state
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural-number bound, $\sigma$ a register state, and $q$ a rational number. If every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$ and $q=0$, then the universal probabilistic program started in the rejection state with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
replaced:
For a bit-string input $x$, register bound $B$, register state $\sigma$, and rational
number $q$, if every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$ and $q=0$, then the universal
probabilistic program started in the rejection state with register state $\sigma$ has
probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
